title: Derived and naive cup products for a morphism of ringed topoi
statement:
Work on sites small in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with commutative ring sheaves. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and the canonical cup morphism $c_{E,F}:Rf_*E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Rf_*F\to Rf_*(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F)$ of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product]. Write $[M]$ for localization of a complex, $\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes N)$ for the signed direct-sum tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], $\rho_{M,N}:[M]\otimes^{\mathbf L}[N]\to[\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes N)]$ for the canonical derived-to-ordinary tensor comparison induced by K-flat resolution augmentations, and $\beta_M:[f_*M]\to Rf_*[M]$ for the canonical comparison obtained by a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For arbitrary unbounded complexes $M,N$ of $R$-modules, let $\nu_{M,N}:\operatorname{Tot}(f_*M\otimes_S f_*N)\to f_*\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes_R N)$ be the naive cochain map: on each $(i,j)$ summand it is the ordinary section tensor map followed by $f_*$ of the tensor summand inclusion. Then the following equality holds in $D(S)$, as maps from $[f_*M]\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}[f_*N]$ to $Rf_*[\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes_R N)]$:
$$Rf_*(\rho_{M,N})\circ c_{[M],[N]}\circ(\beta_M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\beta_N)=\beta_{\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes N)}\circ[\nu_{M,N}]\circ\rho_{f_*M,f_*N}.$$
In particular, this applies to $f_* = \Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$ with $S=\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$ on the point topos, without a final object of $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: Put $A=f_*M$, $B=f_*N$, $V=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_S B)$ and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes_RN)$. Write $L=Lf^*$, $\alpha_X:L[X]\to[f^*X]$, and $e_X:f^*f_*X\to X$ for the ordinary counit. Use the canonical adjunction $L\dashv Rf_*$. It suffices to compare the adjuncts with target $[T]$. The naive map $\nu:V\to f_*T$ is a chain map: on the $(i,j)$ summand naturality of the section tensor map commutes separately with $d_M\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_N$, and both totals use the same sign $(-1)^i$. Its construction uses only maps into $f_*T$ from individual summands, never commutation of $f_*$ with infinite sums.

For every source complex $X$, the canonical derived adjunction satisfies $\varepsilon_{[X]}\circ L(\beta_X)=[e_X]\circ\alpha_{f_*X}$. Indeed apply the representative Hom formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to the ordinary module adjunction, taking $K=X$, $M=f_*X$ and both quasi-isomorphisms $s,t$ and the map $f$ to be identities. The representing cocone component $p_{1_X}$ is $\beta_X$, the cone component $u_{1_{f_*X}}$ is $\alpha_{f_*X}$, and the ordinary adjunct of the identity is $e_X$. Thus the formula gives exactly the asserted equality. These are the resolving cones of the canonical K-flat/K-injective adjunction, rather than an independently chosen adjunction.

proof.text:
By the defining adjunct of the cup product and naturality of $\mu$, the adjunct $a$ of the left side of the required equality is
$$a=\rho_{M,N}\circ\bigl((\varepsilon_{[M]}\circ L\beta_M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}(\varepsilon_{[N]}\circ L\beta_N)\bigr)\circ\mu_{[A],[B]}.$$
Insert Step 2. Naturality of $\rho$ for the chain maps $e_M,e_N$ then gives
$$a=[\operatorname{Tot}(e_M\otimes e_N)]\circ\rho_{f^*A,f^*B}\circ(\alpha_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}\alpha_B)\circ\mu_{[A],[B]}.$$
Here naturality of $\rho$ is the augmentation naturality of the K-flat tensor construction: resolve the maps, tensor their commuting augmentation squares, and localize; the resolution identifications are those of the tensor descent node.

Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-pullback-derived-ordinary-tensor] to $A,B$. Step 3 becomes
$$a=[\operatorname{Tot}(e_M\otimes e_N)\circ\delta_{A,B}]\circ\alpha_V\circ L(\rho_{A,B}).$$
No ordinary tensor is substituted for a derived tensor by an asserted isomorphism: the possibly noninvertible $\rho$ and $\alpha$ are retained throughout.

The equality of chain maps
$$\operatorname{Tot}(e_M\otimes e_N)\circ\delta_{A,B}=e_T\circ f^*(\nu)$$
follows summand by summand from the ordinary module adjunction. In bidegree $(i,j)$, after inverse image and scalar extension, the two maps send $r\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $r(e_M(1\otimes x)\otimes e_N(1\otimes y))$ in the $(i,j)$ summand of $T$. This is exactly the section tensor pairing defining $\nu$, transposed by the ordinary Hom bijection. The normalized ordinary tensor constraint sends $r\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(r\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. The equality holds on generalized pure tensors and hence after sheafification, and on the direct sum since it holds on every summand. All maps have degree zero, so no factors are interchanged and no additional Koszul sign occurs.

The last expression is the adjunct of the right side. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves the required equality. Finally the definition of global cup product is precisely the ringed-topos morphism to $(\mathrm{pt},\Gamma(\mathcal C,R))$, so the same calculation gives the stated specialization. Its compatible-family definition of global sections does not require a final object in $\mathcal C$.
